newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL IPO timing good, analysts see discount.
newsitem.headline: MOL IPO timing good, analysts see discount.

text.p: Shares of Hungary's oil and gas company MOL are likely to be offered at a small discount from current bourse prices, analysts said on Tuesday, adding that the timing of the IPO was good.
"I would expect the price to be around $16.50," Rudi Voros, of London-based ICE Securities, told Reuters.
APV is placing a 12.5 percent stake in MOL, with a 2.5 percent over-allotment option, to institutional investors privately.
A domestic public offer of a one percent stake, with an over-allotment possibility of another three percent, will start on May 12, with the price expected on May 8.

The news that the domestic offer, originally set at one plus one percent, has been increased to one plus three percent, has somewhat depressed MOL's bourse prices but had little impact on the offering, itself, another analyst said.
"Domestic shareholders started selling MOL, as they expected the offer to be at a discount," said Frances Cloud of London-based Nomura Equity Research.
Voros also said that the extra two percent would make little difference to the issue as a whole.
"One has to look at this from a global liquidity angle," he said. "The $300 million MOL issue is not very significant compared with the amounts flowing into emerging markets".
He added that the timing of the MOL IPO was very good as it coincided with an overall positive sentiment on international markets.
MOL, the share with the highest capitalisation of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) has a registered share capital of 98.4 billion forints.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares stood at 3,175 forints at 0949 GMT.
